genZNote: The species Shiga toxin is literally named after — the most dangerous member of a genus that's already not messing around.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human intestinal tract only — no significant animal reservoir
habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen; very low infectious dose (as few as 10-100 organisms)
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Spread via fecally contaminated food, water, and fomites; can persist where sanitation is poor

culture.media: MacConkey agar, XLD agar, Hektoen enteric agar

identificationClues: H2S negative — helps distinguish from Salmonella on enteric media
Produces Shiga toxin — the most potent toxin among Shigella species, causing the most severe dysentery
Very low infectious dose enables rapid person-to-person spread, especially in crowded/poor-sanitation settings

diseases: Severe bacillary dysentery (bloody, mucoid diarrhea with fever and abdominal cramps)
Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) — a recognized complication due to Shiga toxin
virulenceFactors: Shiga toxin — inhibits protein synthesis in host cells (inactivates the 60S ribosomal subunit), causing direct cytotoxicity and endothelial damage
Invasion of colonic epithelial cells via a Type III secretion system
Very low infectious dose facilitating person-to-person spread
toxins: Shiga toxin (most potent of all Shigella species)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route; contaminated food/water and person-to-person spread, especially in crowded settings with poor sanitation
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Historically associated with the most severe Shigella outbreaks and epidemics, particularly in developing regions and refugee/crowded settings; less common in industrialized countries today
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Non-motile, H2S-negative, non-lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rods on enteric media in a patient with bloody diarrhea should prompt consideration of Shigella, with dysenteriae carrying the highest risk of severe complications

examFacts.importantDisease: Severe bacillary dysentery; risk of hemolytic uremic syndrome
examFacts.importantTest: Stool culture on XLD/Hektoen agar; Shiga toxin detection
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Produces the most potent Shiga toxin among Shigella species, causing the most severe dysentery and a real risk of HUS
